elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted subsection: "The license granted under section 2(a) extends to any affiliate of Client identified in a written notice from Client to TrueLink" — coverage exists, though gated on notice (the fallback formulation rather than automatic preferred coverage).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither section 2(a) nor the inserted subsection mentions contractors or agents acting on Client's behalf; the grant runs to Client (and noticed affiliates) only.
No perpetuity language anywhere; section 2(a) grants a licence "in accordance with this Agreement" with no stated term treatment for paid-up rights.
The word "irrevocable" does not appear; the grant is silent on revocability (the deterministic check only confirms no express at-will revocation remains, not affirmative irrevocability).

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no licence-termination standard tying revocation/termination to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The insertion permits transfer only "to a successor in a merger or acquisition", which is narrower than transferability to Customer's successors generally (e.g. asset sale or reorganisation).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "[T]he license granted under section 2(a) extends to any affiliate of Client identified in a written notice from Client to TrueLink" — express affiliate coverage on written notice; "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so this is new, non-duplicative coverage.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "Client may transfer this license to a successor in a merger or acquisition without TrueLink's approval" — a direct, unconditional Customer-side transfer permission; it does not create any new Vendor assignment exception.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice and an M&A successor transfer right are both in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level remains incomplete — no contractor coverage, no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up language, no breach-only termination standard for the subscription licence, and successor transfer limited to merger or acquisition. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on its behalf", express "perpetual and irrevocable" for paid-up rights, a "terminable only for Client's uncured material breach" limit, and broaden "successor in a merger or acquisition" to Client's successors generally.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletions from section 2(a) or section 15, no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra requirements. "Client" does not already include affiliates, so there is no duplicate coverage, and no separate personnel/access edit was added (correctly, since nothing in the retained grant contradicts affiliate use through authorised personnel).

Intent preserved: the Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/free-to-use-alternatives sentence, the section 2(d) ownership reservation and section 15's general consent requirement all survive. The direct "without TrueLink's approval" formulation is the minimal route and avoids a broad notwithstanding override of section 15; it does not enlarge TrueLink's own assignment rights.

Housekeeping only (not a minimality or intent failure): the new subsection is untitled by letter — give it a letter (e.g. "e.") so it does not collide with the existing 2(d), and note the pre-existing internal mismatch between "section 2.1" in 2(d) and "section 2(a)", which the edit neither created nor worsened.
